ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In quadrilateral \(ABCD\), triangles \(OAB\) and \(OCD\) share the common vertex \(O\), and \( \triangle OAB \cong \triangle OCD\). As shown in Figure 2, points \(B\), \(O\), and \(C\) are not on the same line, and \(\angle AOB=90^\circ\), given that \(AD^2+BC^2=50\), \(AO=3\), find the area of \(\triangle OAB\).
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect $AC, BD$ and they intersect at point Q, \\
$\because$ $\triangle OAB \cong \triangle OCD$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle COD = \angle AOB = 90^\circ$, $OA = OC, OB = OD$, $AB = CD$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle AOC = \angle BOD$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle OAC = \angle OCA = \angle OBD = \angle ODB$. \\
$\because$ $\angle OBC + \angle OCB = 180^\circ - \angle BOC$, $\angle AOD = 180^\circ - \angle BOC$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle OBC + \angle OCB = \angle AOD$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle DQC = \angle QBO + \angle OBC + \angle QCO + \angle OCB$ \\
$= \angle OAC + \angle OCA + \angle AOD$ \\
$= 180^\circ - 90^\circ = 90^\circ$. \\
$\therefore$ $AD^2 = AQ^2 + DQ^2$, $BC^2 = BQ^2 + CQ^2$, \\
$\therefore$ $AD^2 + BC^2 = AQ^2 + DQ^2 + BQ^2 + CQ^2$ \\
$= AB^2 + CD^2$, \\
$\because$ $AB = CD$, \\
$\therefore$ $AD^2 + BC^2 = 2AB^2 = 50$, \\
$\therefore$ $AB = 5$, \\
$\because$ $AO = 3$, \\
$\therefore$ $BO = 4$, \\
$\therefore$ the area of $\triangle OAB = \boxed{6}$.
